events.title: London opens the world's first underground railway
events.summary: The Metropolitan Railway began passenger service between Paddington and Farringdon. Building a railway beneath crowded streets established a new layer of urban transport infrastructure.
events.lesson: When surface space is exhausted, changing the system's geometry can unlock capacity that incremental optimization cannot.

events.title: Boston Molasses Flood: a storage tank fails without warning
events.summary: A large molasses tank ruptured in Boston's North End, releasing a destructive wave through nearby streets. Twenty-one people died and buildings, vehicles and elevated-rail structures were damaged.
events.lesson: Low operating pressure does not mean low consequence; large stored volume, brittle material and weak inspection can create catastrophic energy release.

events.title: Nautilus gets underway on nuclear power
events.summary: USS Nautilus left the pier under nuclear power, becoming the first submarine driven by a nuclear reactor. Its propulsion system removed the need for frequent surfacing to recharge batteries.
events.lesson: A new energy source can change the architecture of an entire system, not merely improve its endurance.
events.source_label: U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command

events.title: Macintosh makes the graphical interface a consumer product
events.summary: Apple released the Macintosh with a mouse-driven graphical interface, a compact integrated display and visual desktop metaphors. It brought interaction methods developed in research laboratories to a mass-market computer.
events.lesson: A technology becomes transformative when hardware, software and interaction design are engineered as one understandable product.

events.title: Apollo 1: a ground test becomes a lethal system test
events.summary: A cabin fire during a launch-pad test killed astronauts Virgil Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee. A high-pressure oxygen atmosphere, combustible materials and a difficult inward-opening hatch made the fire unsurvivable.
events.lesson: A test environment can be more hazardous than the mission. Analyze the complete test configuration as an operational system.

events.title: Challenger: warnings lost in the launch decision
events.summary: Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch. Cold-stiffened O-rings failed to seal a solid rocket booster joint, while earlier engineering concerns had not stopped the launch.
events.lesson: A technical warning is useless if the decision process can overrule it without resolving the uncertainty.

events.title: Explorer 1 turns a first satellite into a discovery
events.summary: The United States launched Explorer 1, its first satellite. James Van Allen's cosmic-ray experiment returned unexpected measurements that led to discovery of the radiation belts around Earth.
events.lesson: A first prototype creates more value when it carries instruments able to reveal what the designers do not yet know.

events.title: Columbia: familiar damage became normal
events.summary: Foam shed from the external tank during launch and breached Columbia's left wing. Superheated gas entered the wing during re-entry, causing the orbiter to break apart.
events.lesson: Repeatedly surviving a defect does not make the defect safe. Treat recurring anomalies as evidence, not reassurance.

events.title: East Palestine: a hot bearing escapes the warning system
events.summary: A failed and overheated wheel bearing caused a Norfolk Southern freight train to derail in Ohio. Hazardous-material tank cars were damaged and the subsequent fire forced evacuation of nearby residents.
events.lesson: Condition monitoring must provide enough detection distance, alarm clarity and response time to stop a degrading component before failure.

events.title: Imperial Sugar: ordinary dust becomes explosive fuel
events.summary: A combustible sugar-dust explosion and fire killed 14 people at the Port Wentworth refinery. Dust had accumulated on surfaces and inside enclosed conveying equipment, allowing the initial event to propagate.
events.lesson: A familiar material can become a high-energy hazard when particle size, concentration, confinement and ignition align.

events.title: The Boeing 747 makes its first flight
events.summary: The prototype 747 took off from Everett for the first time. Developing the large aircraft also required Boeing to create an immense new factory and a production system capable of assembling it.
events.lesson: When scale changes radically, the factory, tooling and logistics become part of the product design.

events.title: Friendship 7 carries an American into orbit
events.summary: John Glenn completed three Earth orbits aboard Friendship 7, becoming the first American to orbit the planet. The flight integrated launch, tracking, life support, re-entry and recovery into one mission.
events.lesson: A complex system is demonstrated only when every interface works across the complete operating cycle.

events.title: The Daventry experiment proves aircraft can be detected by radio
events.summary: Robert Watson-Watt's team detected radio signals reflected from an RAF bomber using transmissions from Daventry. The improvised experiment demonstrated the practical basis for radar-based air defence.
events.lesson: A focused experiment should test the weakest assumption in the proposed system before the full system is built.

events.title: Concorde proves a shared supersonic design
events.summary: The French-built Concorde 001 completed the programme's first flight from Toulouse. The aircraft emerged from a formal British-French partnership spanning companies, governments and engineering teams.
events.lesson: International engineering works when interfaces, authority and configuration control are designed as carefully as the hardware.

events.title: Bell's telephone carries understandable speech
events.summary: Alexander Graham Bell spoke through his experimental telephone and Thomas Watson heard and understood him in the next room. Bell recorded the successful test in his laboratory notebook.
events.lesson: A complete end-to-end demonstration resolves more uncertainty than isolated component performance.

events.title: Fukushima: one hazard defeats several safeguards
events.summary: A major earthquake and tsunami struck Japan and severely affected the Fukushima Daiichi site. Loss of power and cooling contributed to core damage across multiple reactor units.
events.lesson: Redundant equipment is not independent when one external hazard can disable its shared power, access and support systems.

events.title: St. Francis Dam: the foundation becomes the failure
events.summary: The concrete gravity dam failed suddenly during the night, releasing its reservoir through the Santa Clara Valley. Later analysis identified weak geology and sliding at an abutment as central to the failure.
events.lesson: A dam is not only concrete. Its abutments, foundation geology and reservoir slopes are structural components too.

events.title: FIU bridge: calculation errors survive peer review
events.summary: A partially constructed pedestrian bridge collapsed onto an open road in Miami. The NTSB found load-and-capacity calculation errors and an inadequate independent peer review.
events.lesson: When real cracking contradicts the model, stop exposure and challenge the model before continuing work.

events.title: Goddard launches the first liquid-fuel rocket
events.summary: Robert Goddard launched a rocket powered by liquid oxygen and gasoline in Auburn, Massachusetts. The short flight demonstrated a controllable propulsion architecture that could outperform solid propellants.
events.lesson: A modest experiment can validate the architecture that matters, even when its immediate performance looks unimpressive.

events.title: Texas City: good injury numbers hide process risk
events.summary: Explosions at BP's Texas City refinery killed 15 workers and injured 180. The CSB found organizational and safety deficiencies at multiple levels of the company.
events.lesson: Personal-safety statistics cannot reveal whether high-energy process hazards are actually under control.

events.title: Exxon Valdez grounds on Bligh Reef
events.summary: The loaded tanker left its traffic lane to avoid ice and grounded in Prince William Sound. Eight cargo tanks ruptured, producing a major crude-oil spill.
events.lesson: Navigation safety needs layered barriers—route monitoring, rested staffing and effective traffic oversight—not one attentive operator.

events.title: Triangle fire: production controls block emergency escape
events.summary: Fire swept through the Triangle Waist Company factory in New York, killing 146 workers. Inadequate exits, locked access and weak fire protections prevented many occupants from escaping.
events.lesson: Security and production controls must fail safe during an emergency; no routine objective outranks a clear and usable escape path.

events.title: Three Mile Island: controls obscure the plant state
events.summary: A combination of equipment malfunction, misleading indications and operator actions led to a partial core meltdown at Unit 2. The accident exposed serious weaknesses in control-room design and emergency preparation.
events.lesson: An indicator must show what the equipment actually did, not merely that a command was sent.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower turns repetition into speed
events.summary: The tower was completed after two years, two months and five days of work. Thousands of accurately detailed iron parts were prefabricated and assembled with millions of rivets.
events.lesson: Standardized parts and precise workshop drawings can turn an unprecedented structure into repeatable assembly work.

events.title: Tesoro: hidden damage ruptures a heat exchanger
events.summary: A nearly 40-year-old heat exchanger at the Anacortes refinery ruptured during startup, causing an explosion and fire that killed seven workers. High-temperature hydrogen attack had weakened the steel from within.
events.lesson: Damage mechanisms that are hard to inspect require conservative material limits, targeted monitoring and explicit life-cycle management.

events.title: Motorola demonstrates a portable cellular phone
events.summary: Motorola publicly demonstrated a working handheld cellular telephone in New York. The prototype showed that a cellular network could serve a person carrying a device, not only a telephone installed in a car.
events.lesson: Changing where a system boundary sits can transform a service: mobility became a property of the user, not the vehicle.

events.title: Early Bird begins global commercial satellite communications
events.summary: Intelsat I, known as Early Bird, launched into geosynchronous orbit as the first commercial communications satellite of its kind. It connected established ground stations across the Atlantic.
events.lesson: Choosing the right operating architecture can simplify every endpoint; geosynchronous orbit made antennas and service continuity far easier.

events.title: Vostok 1 carries the first human into space
events.summary: Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit of Earth during a 108-minute flight aboard Vostok 1. The mission proved that launch, life support, orbital flight and return could be integrated for a human passenger.
events.lesson: For a first-of-kind mission, success depends on managing the whole sequence—not optimizing any single phase in isolation.

events.title: Titanic: prestige cannot substitute for survivability
events.summary: RMS Titanic sank after striking an iceberg during its maiden voyage, killing about 1,500 people. The disaster drove international changes in lifeboat provision, radio watchkeeping and ice patrols.
events.lesson: Design beyond preventing failure: provide detection, evacuation and rescue capacity for the failure that still occurs.
events.source_label: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

events.title: West Fertilizer: a stored material endangers its neighbors
events.summary: A fire reached roughly 30 tons of fertilizer-grade ammonium nitrate at a storage facility in West, Texas. The resulting explosion killed 15 people, injured more than 260 and damaged nearby homes and schools.
events.lesson: Hazard controls must extend beyond the fence line; inventory, siting, emergency planning and community exposure are one system.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon: warning tests are misread
events.summary: The Macondo well blew out, causing explosions and fire aboard Deepwater Horizon. Investigators found that pressure-test results were misinterpreted and the blowout preventer failed during the emergency.
events.lesson: A safety-critical test needs explicit acceptance criteria and a required response when the result is ambiguous.

events.title: Hubble launches with repair built into the concept
events.summary: Space Shuttle Discovery launched the Hubble Space Telescope. Although a mirror flaw was discovered later, the observatory's serviceable design allowed astronauts to install corrective optics.
events.lesson: For systems that cannot be perfectly verified before deployment, planned access and recoverability are design features.

events.title: Chornobyl: an unsafe test met an unstable reactor
events.summary: Reactor Unit 4 went out of control during a planned low-power test. The resulting explosion and fire destroyed the reactor building and released large amounts of radioactive material.
events.lesson: Safety depends on the plant, the procedure and the organization together. Weakness in all three can align catastrophically.

events.title: The Airbus A380 makes its first flight
events.summary: The double-deck A380 took off from Toulouse for its maiden flight. Its scale required globally distributed manufacturing, specialized transport logistics and carefully controlled assembly interfaces.
events.lesson: At extreme scale, logistics and configuration control become first-class parts of the engineering design.

events.title: Aloha 243: hidden fatigue opens an aircraft in flight
events.summary: A large section of the Boeing 737's upper fuselage separated during flight after lap-joint fatigue and disbonding went undetected. The crew landed the severely damaged aircraft, but one flight attendant was lost.
events.lesson: Inspection intervals and methods must follow actual crack growth, environment and usage—not only the original design-life assumptions.

events.title: CERN releases the Web into the public domain
events.summary: CERN made the World Wide Web software available royalty-free in the public domain. Open access allowed anyone to implement, extend and deploy the protocols without negotiating permission.
events.lesson: For a network technology, open interfaces and permissionless adoption can matter as much as the original invention.

events.title: Empire State Building industrializes the skyscraper
events.summary: The 102-storey Empire State Building officially opened after construction lasting about one year and 45 days. Standardized steelwork, coordinated deliveries and repetitive floor planning sustained exceptional speed.
events.lesson: Schedule breakthroughs come from designing the production system—interfaces, repetition and material flow—not merely making crews work faster.

events.title: The Channel Tunnel connects two national systems
events.summary: The rail tunnel beneath the English Channel officially opened, physically linking Britain and continental Europe. Three parallel tunnels joined works advancing from two countries.
events.lesson: Interfaces between teams deserve the same design attention as the structure itself—geometry, standards and decisions must meet in the middle.

events.title: Sunshine Skyway: a ship strike removes an unprotected pier
events.summary: The bulk carrier Summit Venture struck a bridge support pier during severe weather, collapsing about 1,297 feet of roadway into Tampa Bay. Thirty-five people died as vehicles continued onto the failed span.
events.lesson: Critical supports need impact protection, and sudden structural loss needs an independent way to stop approaching users.

events.title: Two railroads meet at one final interface
events.summary: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines met at Promontory Summit, completing the first transcontinental railroad across the United States. A telegraph announced the final connection nationwide.
events.lesson: Large parallel projects only become one system when their geometry, standards, schedule and final interface agree.

events.title: ValuJet 592: mislabeled components become live hazards
events.summary: ValuJet Flight 592 crashed after improperly prepared chemical oxygen generators activated in the cargo compartment and fed an uncontrollable fire. All 110 people aboard were killed.
events.lesson: A component's hazardous state must remain visible through removal, storage, labeling, contracting and transport.

events.title: Skylab turns damaged hardware into a working space station
events.summary: NASA launched Skylab, the first U.S. space station. Launch damage removed its thermal shield and disabled a solar array, but engineers and astronauts developed repairs that enabled three productive crewed missions.
events.lesson: Recovery capability comes from observable failure states, adaptable procedures and hardware that people can access and repair.

events.title: Ronan Point: a local blast triggers progressive collapse
events.summary: A gas explosion in an 18th-floor flat blew out load-bearing panels, causing one corner of the 22-storey tower to collapse downward. Four people died and 17 were injured.
events.lesson: A robust structure must tolerate local damage without allowing it to propagate into disproportionate collapse.
events.source_label: UK Independent Review of Building Regulations

events.title: The Brooklyn Bridge joins two cities across the East River
events.summary: The Brooklyn Bridge opened between Manhattan and Brooklyn as the world's longest suspension bridge at the time. Its hybrid cable-and-stiffening system carried rail, road and pedestrian traffic.
events.lesson: An unprecedented span succeeds when structural innovation is paired with redundancy, stiffness and a practical operating system.

events.title: The Golden Gate Bridge opens ahead of schedule
events.summary: The bridge opened first to pedestrians, connecting San Francisco and Marin across a difficult strait. It was completed ahead of schedule and under budget.
events.lesson: Ambitious engineering is credible when structural innovation is matched by disciplined construction planning.

events.title: AF447: automation hands back an unclear situation
events.summary: Temporary icing of the Airbus A330's Pitot probes produced unreliable airspeed indications and an autopilot disconnect. The crew did not recognize the resulting stall before the aircraft struck the Atlantic.
events.lesson: Automation handover must leave humans with enough cues, training and time to identify the actual flight state.
events.source_label: French Civil Aviation Safety Investigation Authority

events.title: Ariane 5: reused software meets a new flight envelope
events.summary: Ariane 5 Flight 501 lost guidance and attitude information shortly after launch. An inertial-reference conversion overflowed in software inherited from Ariane 4.
events.lesson: Proven software is only proven inside its validated operating assumptions. Reuse the tests and assumptions, not just the code.

events.title: Teton Dam fails during its first filling
events.summary: Seepage appeared through the embankment as the new reservoir filled. Attempts to plug the leaks failed, internal erosion accelerated and the dam breached catastrophically.
events.lesson: First filling is a commissioning test. Instrumentation, trigger limits and emergency drawdown must be ready before water rises.

events.title: Williams Olefins: standby equipment is isolated from relief
events.summary: A heat exchanger reboiler ruptured at the Geismar plant after being heated while isolated from its pressure-relief path. The explosion killed two workers and injured 167.
events.lesson: Every permitted valve configuration must preserve a safe pressure path, including startup, standby and maintenance states.

events.title: Grenfell: the façade becomes a fire path
events.summary: A kitchen fire escaped into Grenfell Tower's external envelope and spread rapidly around the high-rise. The public inquiry exposed failures across products, testing, regulation and oversight.
events.lesson: Compliance of individual products does not prove the assembled building system will resist fire.
events.source_label: UK Government response to the Grenfell Inquiry

events.title: The Manchester Baby runs a stored program
events.summary: The Small-Scale Experimental Machine successfully executed a program held electronically in its memory. Instructions and data could now share storage and be changed without rewiring the machine.
events.lesson: Moving behavior from wiring into stored information turns a special-purpose machine into a programmable platform.

events.title: Fort Totten: the control system loses a train
events.summary: A Washington Metro train struck the rear of a stopped train after faulty track-circuit modules stopped detecting it and continued transmitting movement commands. Nine people died.
events.lesson: A safety system must treat loss of detection as occupied or unknown—not as evidence that the protected space is clear.

events.title: The Benz Patent Motor Car enters public streets
events.summary: Carl Benz drove his patented three-wheeled motor car publicly around Mannheim. The vehicle combined its engine, fuel system, transmission, chassis and steering as a purpose-built road machine rather than a motorized carriage.
events.lesson: A new product category emerges when its subsystems are designed around the new purpose instead of attached to the old architecture.

events.title: Piper Alpha: maintenance status is lost at handover
events.summary: A condensate pump was restarted while its pressure-safety valve was absent for maintenance, allowing gas to escape and ignite. Escalating fires destroyed the offshore platform.
events.lesson: Equipment status must survive every shift change. A permit system is a safety barrier only when operations can see and trust it.

events.title: Seveso: a runaway reaction spreads beyond the plant
events.summary: An uncontrolled reaction in a trichlorophenol process released a toxic cloud containing dioxin near Seveso, Italy. Widespread contamination led Europe to create major-accident control legislation bearing the town's name.
events.lesson: Runaway protection, release containment and off-site planning must be designed together when a process can affect the surrounding community.

events.title: Mariner 4 returns the first close-up image of Mars
events.summary: Mariner 4 transmitted the first close-range images of another planet after an eight-month journey. Its limited communications link returned image data line by line across interplanetary distance.
events.lesson: When bandwidth is scarce, disciplined encoding, storage and error-tolerant transmission can deliver information more valuable than raw data volume.

events.title: Hyatt walkways: a small detail doubles the load
events.summary: Two suspended walkways collapsed into the hotel atrium. The box-beam and hanger-rod connections lacked sufficient load capacity after a critical connection detail was changed.
events.lesson: A detail change is a design change. Recalculate the complete load path before approving it.

events.title: Apollo 11 lands humans on the Moon
events.summary: After a four-day journey, Apollo 11's lunar module landed in the Sea of Tranquility. The mission integrated propulsion, navigation, computing, communications and human judgement.
events.lesson: Systems engineering succeeds when independently difficult subsystems are designed around one shared mission.

events.title: Concorde 4590: runway debris crosses system boundaries
events.summary: Concorde Flight 4590 crashed after striking a metal strip on the runway. Tire fragments damaged a fuel tank, released fuel ignited and the aircraft lost thrust shortly after takeoff.
events.lesson: Trace high-energy debris paths across subsystem boundaries; a small external object can defeat several protections in sequence.
events.source_label: French Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis

events.title: A durable telegraph cable connects the Atlantic
events.summary: The 1866 expedition completed a reliable submarine telegraph cable between Europe and North America after earlier cables failed. Messages that had taken days or weeks could cross the ocean in minutes.
events.lesson: After first-of-kind failure, improve the complete deployment system—materials, handling, testing, repair and recovery—not only the headline component.
events.source_label: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

events.title: I-35W bridge: an original design error meets added load
events.summary: The Minneapolis bridge collapsed during evening traffic, killing 13 people. The NTSB found undersized gusset plates from the original design, combined with increased dead load and concentrated construction loads.
events.lesson: Reassess the complete load path when permanent weight or temporary construction loads change—not only the modified components.

events.title: The IBM PC makes an open component ecosystem mainstream
events.summary: IBM introduced its Personal Computer using commercially available components and published technical information that enabled compatible hardware and software. The architecture rapidly became an industry standard.
events.lesson: A platform can scale faster when clear interfaces let other organizations add value without redesigning the core system.

events.title: The Panama Canal opens a controlled water route
events.summary: The steamship Ancon made the official opening transit through the Panama Canal. Locks, dams, an artificial lake and major excavations created a navigable route between two oceans.
events.lesson: Transformative infrastructure often succeeds by controlling the environment as a system rather than overpowering one obstacle.

events.title: The Mini turns packaging into the innovation
events.summary: The British Motor Corporation unveiled Alec Issigonis's compact Mini. Its transverse engine and front-wheel-drive layout devoted far more of the vehicle footprint to people and luggage.
events.lesson: When space is fixed, question the architecture before optimizing the individual components.

events.title: Comair 5191: the aircraft departs from the wrong runway
events.summary: The crew lined up on Lexington's short, unlit runway 26 instead of the assigned runway 22. The aircraft overran the runway during takeoff, killing 49 of the 50 people aboard.
events.lesson: For irreversible actions, independently verify position against the intended configuration rather than relying on expectation and visual familiarity.

events.title: Swissair 111: hidden fire outruns diagnosis and diversion
events.summary: An in-flight fire spread through flammable materials above the cockpit ceiling of Swissair Flight 111. Critical systems failed before the crew could land, and all 229 people aboard died.
events.lesson: Smoke of unknown origin is a time-critical system failure; materials, detection and procedures must assume that hidden fire can accelerate.

events.title: Jack Kilby demonstrates a working integrated circuit
events.summary: Texas Instruments engineer Jack Kilby demonstrated an electronic circuit whose components were formed on one piece of semiconductor material. Integration replaced many discrete parts and their individual connections.
events.lesson: Reliability and scale improve when interfaces disappear; integrating components can remove more failure opportunities than perfecting each connection.

events.title: Mars Climate Orbiter: one interface, two unit systems
events.summary: NASA lost contact as the spacecraft reached Mars. The navigation error came from one part of the system supplying English units where another expected metric units.
events.lesson: Units are part of an interface contract. Make them explicit, machine-checkable and impossible to ignore.

events.title: Hoover Dam integrates water, power and construction
events.summary: President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicated the immense concrete arch-gravity dam. The project combined river diversion, flood control, water storage and hydroelectric generation at unprecedented scale.
events.lesson: Megaproject value comes from integrating operating purposes early, not adding disconnected functions after construction.

events.title: Sputnik begins the space age
events.summary: The Soviet Union placed the first artificial satellite into Earth orbit. The small radio transmitter demonstrated an entirely new technological capability to the world.
events.lesson: A simple, working demonstration can change an entire field more decisively than a grand unfinished system.

events.title: Vajont: the dam survives but the system fails
events.summary: A vast landslide entered the Vajont reservoir and displaced a wave over the dam into the valley below. The concrete dam itself remained largely intact while communities downstream were destroyed.
events.lesson: Passing the structural check is not enough when hazards outside the structure can dominate the system consequence.

events.title: The Bell X-1 breaks the sound barrier
events.summary: Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 beyond Mach 1 in controlled level flight. Its thin, bullet-shaped body and all-moving horizontal tail addressed the severe aerodynamic changes near sonic speed.
events.lesson: When a regime change invalidates familiar controls, redesign around the new physics instead of forcing the old architecture harder.

events.title: Aberfan: an unmanaged waste tip becomes a landslide
events.summary: A saturated coal-waste tip slid down the hillside into the Welsh village of Aberfan, engulfing a school and homes. The disaster killed 144 people, including 116 children.
events.lesson: Waste storage is an engineered structure: drainage, geology, loading history and downstream exposure require ownership and continuous control.

events.title: ARPANET's first message crashes after two letters
events.summary: A UCLA team attempted to send LOGIN to a computer at Stanford Research Institute. The remote system crashed after receiving LO, but the connection was restored and the full command followed.
events.lesson: The first useful systems test is small, end-to-end and allowed to fail where the interfaces are real.

events.title: Tacoma Narrows: static strength was not enough
events.summary: Only four months after opening, the slender suspension bridge collapsed in wind. Its deck entered a self-excited torsional motion that the original design approach did not control.
events.lesson: A structure must be stable under dynamic interaction with its environment, not merely strong under static loads.

events.title: Apollo 4 tests the complete Saturn V at once
events.summary: NASA launched the first Saturn V on Apollo 4 using an all-up configuration with all three stages live. The mission tested propulsion, staging, spacecraft systems and high-speed re-entry in one integrated flight.
events.lesson: Integrated testing exposes interface behavior that isolated qualification cannot, when the risk is understood and the instrumentation is ready.

events.title: The Intel 4004 makes computing programmable
events.summary: Intel introduced the 4004 general-purpose programmable microprocessor. Functions that previously required custom hardware could now be implemented by mass-produced silicon and software.
events.lesson: A powerful abstraction moves complexity from specialized hardware into a reusable platform.

events.title: King's Cross: a small escalator fire becomes a fireball
events.summary: A fire beneath a wooden escalator at King's Cross Underground station suddenly intensified and spread into the ticket hall, killing 31 people. The inquiry produced extensive changes to materials, procedures and fire management.
events.lesson: Do not classify a hazard by its familiar beginning; geometry, concealed fuel and airflow can create a rapid transition to a different regime.

events.title: Zarya begins construction of the International Space Station
events.summary: The Zarya control module launched as the first element of the International Space Station. It provided early power, propulsion and control while later modules from multiple nations assembled around shared interfaces.
events.lesson: A long-lived modular system begins with stable interfaces and an initial element that can support incomplete configurations.

events.title: Chicago Pile-1 sustains a controlled chain reaction
events.summary: Enrico Fermi's team achieved the first self-sustaining, controlled nuclear chain reaction beneath the stands of the University of Chicago's Stagg Field.
events.lesson: A breakthrough experiment should make the critical variable observable and controllable—not merely prove that the reaction can occur.

events.title: Buncefield: independent shutdown fails with the gauge
events.summary: A gasoline storage tank overflowed, forming a large vapor cloud that exploded at the Buncefield depot. The level gauge had stuck and the independent high-level shutdown did not prevent overfilling.
events.lesson: A protection layer is independent only if its sensing, logic, actuation and failure modes do not share the initiating fault.

events.title: The Wright Flyer achieves controlled powered flight
events.summary: Orville Wright flew for 12 seconds and 120 feet at Kitty Hawk. The deeper achievement was three-axis control, developed through years of experiments and iterative testing.
events.lesson: Solve controllability, not just raw performance. A machine that cannot be controlled has not solved the problem.

events.title: T2 Laboratories: cooling loss triggers a runaway reaction
events.summary: A reactor exploded at T2 Laboratories in Jacksonville, killing four people and injuring 32. Inadequate understanding of the reaction hazards left the process unable to control a rapid temperature and pressure rise after cooling failed.
events.lesson: Scale-up requires reaction calorimetry and a safe response to cooling loss; normal operating data cannot define the runaway boundary.

events.title: EBR-I produces usable electricity from nuclear fission
events.summary: Experimental Breeder Reactor I generated enough electricity to illuminate four 200-watt lamps, the first usable electrical power produced by nuclear fission. It later supplied electricity to its entire building.
events.lesson: A small end-to-end demonstration can prove energy conversion and control before scaling the plant around it.

events.title: Webb launches folded for a million-kilometre journey
events.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope launched aboard Ariane 5 toward its operating region around the Sun-Earth L2 point. Its mirror and sunshield then deployed through a long sequence of planned steps.
events.lesson: When repair is impractical, deployment reliability comes from controlled sequence design, extensive testing and observable state transitions.

events.title: Eastern 401: a small indicator captures the whole cockpit
events.summary: While the crew investigated a landing-gear indication, the autopilot was inadvertently disconnected and the aircraft descended unnoticed into the Florida Everglades. The crash became a catalyst for crew resource management.
events.lesson: Troubleshooting must never consume the function that keeps the system safe; assign one person and one instrument loop to guard the primary state.
